channelTitle: Forget your morning coffee, Grandma June roasted this weed from the yard instead
hook: Forget your morning coffee, Grandma June used to roast a weed straight from the yard instead.
remedy: As an old-fashioned piece of home wisdom, dandelion roots dug up, cleaned, roasted until deep brown, and then brewed like coffee grounds were an old way to enjoy a warm, bitter cup believed to ease digestion without the caffeine jitters.
steps: Dig up dandelion roots, scrub them clean, and slice into small pieces
Roast the pieces in a dry pan or low oven until dark brown and fragrant
Grind the roasted root and brew it like coffee grounds, steeping in hot water for several minutes before straining
caution: Skip this if you have gallbladder problems or take diuretic medication, since dandelion root can act as a mild diuretic. Only harvest roots from areas you know are free of pesticides.
cta: Have you ever tried roasted dandelion root, or does real coffee stay non-negotiable for you? Tell Grandma June in the comments.
